paragraphs: He was R' Yose son of R' Chanina’s attendant, Bava Batra 90b. Dikdukei Soferim reads Suga; Hyman says Seder HaDorot needlessly split him into two people.[^1]

notes.text: שמעיה is read as attendant/personal servant, not the name Shemaiah. כב״ב is contextually read as a Bava Batra locator and צ: as 90b under the colon convention, without independent edition verification. דק״ס and סה״ד are read as Dikdukei Soferim and Seder HaDorot. Hyman attributes Suga and criticizes the needless split from Puga; no new collation or canonical identity merger follows. The source’s two personal-title abbreviations, including the father’s, remain R'.
